headline: GOLD CRACKS $4,000 FLOOR — IRAN WAR FUELS INFLATION FEARS, BOND YIELDS WIN OVER SAFE-HAVEN BID
snippet: Gold closed below $4,000 on July 17 for the first time since late June, logging a 3%-plus weekly loss in a market paradox: US-Iran airstrikes that sent Brent past $84 and drove oil up nearly 13% over five days are fuelling inflation fears and rate-hike bets — pushing a 51% probability of a September Fed increase — which make non-yielding gold less attractive even as geopolitical risk mounts. Bond yields are overriding the safe-haven bid that war normally triggers, because the same oil-price shock that should drive gold higher is simultaneously stoking inflation expectations that strengthen the dollar and raise the opportunity cost of holding bullion. Gold has now shed roughly 29% from its January record near $5,589.

headline: CRESCAT BACKS CANTEX NORTH RACKLA YUKON DRILL — C$3M Raise Funds Active Silver-Germanium Massive Sulphide Program (TSXV:CD)
source_name: Investing News Network / Cantex Mine Development Corp.
snippet: Cantex Mine Development (TSXV: CD) announced on July 17 a non-brokered private placement of up to C$3 million, with Crescat Capital — one of the best-known sector-focused resource funds — increasing its strategic stake through the offering. Proceeds fund active drilling on Cantex's 100%-owned, 14,000-hectare North Rackla project in the Yukon, where more than 100,000 metres of prior drilling has defined 2.8 kilometres of strike and at least 700 metres of vertical depth of high-grade silver-lead-zinc-germanium massive sulphide mineralization. Germanium is a federally designated critical mineral essential for semiconductors and defence electronics, adding strategic appeal to the project beyond its precious and base metals content.

headline: AZTEC DRILLS 155.4m OF 1.63 g/t AUEQ AT TOMBSTONE — Oxide Gold-Silver Zone Doubles Depth, Extends 300m West and South, Arizona (TSXV:AZT)
snippet: Aztec Minerals (TSXV: AZT) released 11 new reverse-circulation holes from its Tombstone Property in southeastern Arizona, with the best intersection returning 155.4 metres at 1.08 g/t Au and 30.23 g/t Ag (1.63 g/t AuEq) from the Contention zone — within a broader 198.1-metre envelope grading 0.86 g/t AuEq. Step-out drilling more than doubled the zone's vertical extent and extended it 300 metres to the west and south, with mineralization remaining open in multiple directions. The oxide, shallow nature of the system points toward heap-leach amenability; Aztec has already engaged Kappes, Cassiday & Associates to advance bottle-roll metallurgical testing, and 26 additional holes remain pending assay.

headline: MONEYMETALS: THE BULLISH CASE FOR SILVER — 6 Straight Deficit Years; LBMA Consensus $79/oz Stands Far Above $56 Spot
snippet: Money Metals Exchange argues that silver's 7% weekly drop to eight-month lows is a cyclical shakeout rather than a structural breakdown, pointing to six consecutive years of supply deficit, China's reclassification of silver as a strategic material effective January 1, 2026, and a consensus among major institutions that the metal is undervalued at current levels: the LBMA's 2026 forecast survey consensus sits at $79.57/oz, JPMorgan's base case is $81, HSBC forecasts $75, and Goldman Sachs puts $85-$100 as achievable. Industrial demand from solar panels and EVs continues to structurally outpace mining supply growth, and the article contends that any normalisation of Fed rhetoric or dollar weakness is likely to reaccelerate the secular bull market.

headline: BOAT COMPANY PIVOTS TO GREENLAND NICKEL — Twin Vee/USFM Merge to Advance 3,020km² Ni-Cu-Co-PGE District; $30M Drill Already Running
snippet: USFM Corporation announced on July 16 a definitive agreement to merge with Nasdaq-listed Twin Vee PowerCats (VEEE) — a recreational boat maker — that will see the combined company focus exclusively on advancing the Disko-Nuussuaq Project in West Greenland, one of the world's largest underexplored magmatic nickel-copper-cobalt-PGE districts at 3,020 km². Twin Vee's marine business will be privatized prior to close; the combined company targets a NYSE American listing in Q3 2026. USFM is already in a US$30 million earn-in agreement with AIM-listed project operator 80 Mile plc, with US$10 million committed for the current season and two rigs actively drilling since July 1 near Qullissat on Disko Island.

headline: CAMECO CIGAR LAKE RESUMES AFTER McCLEAN MILL ACID PLANT FIXED — 2026 U3O8 Guidance 17.5-18M Lbs Unchanged (TSX:CCO)
snippet: Cameco (TSX/NYSE: CCO) confirmed that Cigar Lake Mine in northern Saskatchewan has resumed production following a suspension that began July 1, when Orano's adjacent McClean Lake mill — the only facility licensed to process Cigar Lake ore — shut down to repair its sulfuric acid plant. The mill is now operational, stockpiled ore is flowing, and Cameco's full-year production guidance of 17.5-18.0 million pounds of U3O8 (100% basis) remains intact. Uranium spot prices were holding near US$85 per pound ahead of the restart, with the market watching to see whether the brief supply interruption tightens the spot book heading into the fall reactor-fuelling season.

headline: BRIEN LUNDIN: MINING STOCKS LAGGING GOLD IS A GENERATIONAL OPPORTUNITY — 'Still Only in the Second Inning'; First Time Equities Trail Record Metal
snippet: Gold Newsletter publisher Brien Lundin argues that the current setup — where gold has soared to records while silver and mining equities dramatically lag — is historically unprecedented and creates one of the best risk-adjusted entry points in the sector's history. In every prior gold bull market, silver and miners led the metal; the fact that they have not yet done so means the most explosive leg of the rally remains ahead, with mining equities still priced as if gold is at $2,500 rather than $4,000. He views the current washout as a short-term positioning shakeout, not a fundamental breakdown, and urges investors to buy the dips with a multi-quarter horizon as institutional capital begins to re-rate the sector.

headline: GOLD SWOT: DPM METALS BEATS Q2 ESTIMATES BY 31% AT VARES — 102,000 GEOs; Shutdown Done in 7 Days vs 20; $49M Buyback
snippet: This week's VanEck Gold SWOT on GoldSeek highlights DPM Metals' Q2 2026 production beat as the week's top Strength: the company produced 102,000 gold-equivalent ounces in the quarter, with Vares — its newest mine — processing 117,000 tonnes (up 48% quarter-over-quarter) and beating Canaccord's estimate by 31% after completing a planned plant shutdown in just 7 days versus the scheduled 20. Chelopech contributed ~56,000 GEOs and Ada Tepe ~11,000. DPM Metals also repurchased over $49 million of its own shares in the quarter and separately announced the Brevene South porphyry discovery in June, providing a longer-term organic growth option alongside the outperforming operating base.

headline: RIO TINTO BACKS AZIMUT JAMES BAY LITHIUM PEGMATITES — All 5 Maiden Holes Hit Spodumene; Best 1.87% Li2O Over 36m; 340 Samples Average 1.94% (TSXV:AZM)
snippet: Azimut Exploration (TSXV: AZM) released results from its maiden 5-hole, 650-metre diamond drill program at Wabamisk East in the Eeyou Istchee James Bay region of Quebec — entirely funded by Rio Tinto Exploration Canada Inc. All five holes intersected high-grade spodumene pegmatite, with the best intersection returning 1.87% Li2O over 36.30 metres. Surface channel and grab sampling across the Lithos North and South areas has produced 340 samples grading above 0.5% Li2O with a 1.94% average, indicating a multi-kilometre-scale, drill-ready pegmatite field. Rio Tinto's continued commitment as sole funder underscores institutional confidence in the James Bay lithium district as one of North America's premier undeveloped pegmatite terranes.

headline: U.S. RARE EARTH STOCKS UP 81% IN H1 2026 — Germanium +27%, Dysprosium +25% in July; Second Straight Supply Deficit vs EV and Wind Demand
snippet: U.S. rare earth equities surged 81% in the first half of 2026, driven by a trifecta of policy support (Project Vault's $12 billion strategic reserve program), physical price gains (all 18 tracked elements rose in July, led by germanium at +27.8% domestic and dysprosium at +25.4%), and a second consecutive year of structural supply deficit against EV motor and wind turbine demand. The gains unwound partially after June 30, with USAR shares down more than 20% in early July, illustrating the sector's volatility. MP Materials — operator of the Mountain Pass mine — remains the only active U.S. rare earth producer, while USA Rare Earth advances its Oklahoma heavy rare earth project toward production with federal financing backing.
